title: Why salt melts ice on winter roads
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why do they put salt on roads?
Why doesn't road salt work when it's very cold?

explain.say: Pure water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius. But dissolve salt in it and the water has to get colder before it will freeze.

draw.text: Why salt melts ice on winter roads

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a salt crystal lattice. Look at the sodium ion, the chloride ion and the ionic bond. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: Why salt melts ice on winter roads

explain.say: The salt particles get in the way of water molecules trying to lock together into ice. Sea water, with about 3.5 percent salt, freezes at about minus 2 degrees.

On a road, salt dissolves in the thin film of water on the ice. That salty water will not freeze, so the ice touching it melts, and more salt dissolves. Rock salt works well down to about minus 9 degrees.
The more salt, the lower the freezing point, down to about minus 21 degrees for the saltiest mixture. Below that, salt cannot help, so very cold places use grit or other chemicals.

faq.a: Salt dissolves in the thin layer of water that is always on ice. Salty water has a lower freezing point, so the ice in contact with it melts, even below 0 degrees Celsius.
asks: Why does salt make ice melt?

faq.q: Why doesn't road salt work when it's very cold?
faq.a: Below about minus 9 degrees Celsius, rock salt melts ice too slowly to be useful, and below about minus 21 it cannot melt it at all. Then grit or calcium chloride is used instead.
asks: Is there a temperature salt stops working?

faq.q: Why doesn't the sea freeze as easily as lakes?
faq.a: Sea water is salty, so it freezes at about minus 2 degrees instead of 0. The sea also holds a lot of heat and keeps moving.
asks: Why is the sea harder to freeze?

faq.a: Yes. Melting takes heat, so salted ice pulls heat from around it and the mixture gets colder than 0 degrees. Old ice cream makers used ice and salt for exactly this reason.
asks: Why use ice and salt to make ice cream?

faq.q: Is road salt bad for cars and plants?
faq.a: It can be. Salty water makes car bodies rust faster and can harm plants and soil along roadsides, so councils try not to use more than they need.

facts: Sea water, about 3.5 percent salt, freezes at about minus 2 degrees Celsius.
The coldest a salt and water mixture can stay liquid is about minus 21 degrees Celsius.

quiz.why: Salt lowers the freezing point of water, so water on the road stays liquid instead of turning into ice.
